doc: Cells confirmed, via live verification, to have NO real path forward -- the gap tool's own heuristics would otherwise keep re-flagging these as 'sourced-not-built'/'walled'/'no source known' on every regeneration, costing real investigation time to re-derive the same answer. Each entry needs: state, county (or null for every county in that state), column, reason (specific, falsifiable), confirmed_date, confidence ('high' = directly verified for this exact cell; 'medium' = inferred from a verified sibling/structural rule, not independently re-checked for every county it covers). gap_matrix.py's roll_up() checks this registry before finalizing each cell's gap_class and overrides to 'declined (<reason>)' when found -- never silently; the override is itself visible in the gap list so a human can challenge it. A declined entry is a claim, not a law: if new evidence contradicts one (the underlying platform adds a field, a law changes, a county switches vendors), remove or correct the entry and re-verify live before trusting the correction.

Its only bulk GIS layer (Pickens_Open_data FeatureServer/6) has no value field of any kind; its alternate platform (Catalis/Sturgis) only extracts Appraised/Assessed and its CDN API returns a live HTTP 403 (confirmed CatalisBlocked wall).

Its tax card's 'Land Market Value' vs 'Land Use Value' split looks like an ag-deferral field but live-checking 5 real parcel cards showed the split appears on ordinary RESIDENTIAL IMPROVED parcels too (not just FARM VACANT) -- it's a structural artifact of the acreage-valuation schedule (any parcel with a Gross Acres land record gets both numbers), not an ag-rollback flag. No 'Deferred'/'Rollback' label exists on the card. Would need an ACTUAL deferred/rollback label to change this, not a re-derivation from the Market/Use split.

Both GIS hosts (gis2.orangeburgcounty.org, arcserver2.orangeburgcounty.org) have been down/connection-refused for 13+ days (re-confirmed 2026-10-21, not a blip); qPublic is CAPTCHA-walled; the only live AGOL replica has owner/mailing/acreage only, no value or land-use field.

Its cached TOTBDGVAL (building-value-only) field looked like a clean $0=vacant signal (35% of parcels), but a live satellite spot-check against real addresses found actual rooftops on 2 of 7 checked $0 parcels -- almost certainly manufactured/mobile homes taxed as separate personal property, excluded from the real-property improvement-value card. Wiring TOTBDGVAL as vacant_lot here would mis-flag real improved homes. Would need Florence's personal-property/mobile-home tax roll (a different, unbuilt source) to fix, not a reuse of this field.

The only text field (DESCRIPTIO) tested 0/120,547 matches against a VACANT/VAC wordlist -- it's a short legal description, never a land-use class. The RATIO field is a bare SC assessment-ratio code with no companion improvement-value field to anchor a vacant-lot inference against.

South Carolina marriage licenses are issued and recorded by the county PROBATE COURT, never the Register of Deeds, statewide (state law, not county discretion) -- confirmed directly for Sumter (live-pulled its full 182-code CountyFusion/GovOS instrument-type tree: zero marriage-related codes) and corroborated by SCDHEC + Sumter's own Probate Court page. This is structurally different from NC, where RODs DO record marriage licenses (why the Johnston NC EagleWeb sweep worked). This project's ROD-platform infrastructure (sc_countyfusion.py, kofile.py, publicsearch.py, etc.) cannot reach Probate Court records at all -- a different county office entirely, not a missing filter. DIRECTLY verified only for Sumter; HIGH confidence it generalizes (state law), but not independently re-checked county-by-county.
